summary: cors-update typosquats expressjs/cors and fetches remote JavaScript for in-process eval
details: cors-update@2.8.0 impersonates the `expressjs/cors` middleware — package.json reuses the real project's repository, author, description, and keywords, and the source file appends a malicious `getPlugin` export to an otherwise-faithful copy of cors. When a consumer uses the module as a CORS middleware factory, `getPlugin` issues an `https.get` to the hardcoded lookalike domain `api.avax-test.dev` (typosquat of `api.avax-test.network`) with `rejectUnauthorized: false`, then passes the response body to `new Function('require', data)(require)`, evaluating attacker-controlled JavaScript inside the Node process with access to the caller's `require`. TLS verification is disabled on the fetch, so the payload can also be substituted by any on-path attacker. The result is remote code execution in the installer's application whenever the middleware is invoked.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
